old: Twelve people have walked on the Moon, and they did it in eight suits of the same family: the **Apollo A7L** (Apollo 11, 12, 14) and its successor the **A7LB** (Apollo 15, 16, 17). A7L was a one-piece pressure garment with a Hard Upper Torso, soft fabric arms and legs, integrated lunar-overboots, an over-the-shoulder PLSS backpack, and an Oxygen Purge System (OPS) as emergency reserve mounted above the PLSS. Operating pressure was 3.7 psi (0.26 atm) of pure oxygen — the lowest of any flown spacesuit, traded against maximum mobility for walking. The A7LB added a waist-joint convolution that let astronauts sit in the Lunar Roving Vehicle without fighting the suit; without that joint the J-mission EVAs would not have been possible.
